rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation is a prophetic gift because dreams convey divine revelation through symbols that require skill to interpret.
rows.anchor: dreams are a means of divine revelation in which facts appear in symbolic form

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob inferred from Joseph’s dream that Joseph would be a prophet and that Jacob would receive the skill to understand dreams and fulfil God's intent.
rows.anchor: When Jacob (sws) realized that this dream was giving glad tidings of prophethood to Joseph (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor named here is religion and divine law; worldly favors are supplementary, while religion completes God's favors.
rows.anchor: The favour referred to in the verse is that of religion and sharī‘ah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Joseph narrative begins here as an answer to questions about prophetic preaching that troubled both the Prophet's companions and opponents.
rows.anchor: It was not meant to be narrated for the mere sake of narration: its purpose was to answer many questions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section closes by affirming that God can bring His plan to completion, although most people fail to recognize this.
rows.anchor: At the end of this section, it is stated that God is fully capable of realizing His scheme but most people do not know this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening verse warns readers not to treat the account as a mere story; it addresses questions arising during Muhammad's preaching.
rows.anchor: This verse sounds a warning before the narration of the actual anecdote

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story illustrates truth's eventual dominance over falsehood amid Arabia's prevailing disbelief and the Prophet's persecution.
rows.anchor: the topic of the dominance of the truth and humiliation of falsehood has been mentioned in various styles

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account reassures listeners that God’s majesty appears through plans and intentions that ultimately come to pass.
rows.anchor: God’s majesty manifests itself in this way too and all his projects and intentions materialize.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṣabah means a cohesive faction, especially one bound by blood relations.
rows.anchor: especially one which is formed from blood relations and thus is cohesive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In tribal societies without an organized state, families relied on their own strength for defense and support; a large cohort of young men brought influence.
rows.anchor: a tribe and family would depend on its own strength for its support and defence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ is used literally for a state of affairs becoming sound, worries disappearing, and inner discomfort easing.
rows.anchor: The word ﺻﺎﻟﺢhere is used in its literal meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes the scheme Joseph's brothers devised against him.
rows.anchor: The verse points to the scheme plotted by the brothers of Joseph (sws).

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some interpret the brothers' proposal as a plan to repent after committing the crime; Islahi rejects this as grammatically and contextually untenable.
rows.anchor: Some people interpret the sentence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' spite arose from Joseph's emerging virtues, which drew Jacob's love, rather than merely from his status as a half-brother; their failure to target Benjamin supports this.
rows.anchor: The real cause of this spite was not because he was their step brother but because of his high qualities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers believed their numbers sustained the family faction and its dominance, so they viewed Jacob's preference for Joseph and Benjamin as foolish.
rows.anchor: they reckoned that it was because of them that their faction and group existed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A strong tribal family could assume leadership of its tribe or nation.
rows.anchor: would assume the leadership of their tribe or nation and would rule

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about eating and playing subtly suggests a picnic, a popular form of recreation in ancient rural societies and one celebrated by classical Arab poets.
rows.anchor: However, it very subtly signifies a picnic. In ancient rural societies, this was a very popular means of entertainment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wolves were common in nearby areas and sometimes attacked people; Jacob let Joseph go with his brothers reluctantly after their assurances.
rows.anchor: It is evident from this verse that a lot of wolves were found in the adjoining areas

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional passage compresses several events beneath its answer, alluding to the full episode while keeping attention on its central point.
rows.anchor: many things are subsumed under this conditional particle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers disagreed over killing Joseph or abandoning him in a well.
rows.anchor: there existed a difference of opinion among the brothers of Joseph (sws) about killing him or throwing him in the well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers ultimately accepted the proposal to put Joseph in the well rather than kill him.
rows.anchor: finally the latter option prevailed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “revelation” means an implanted thought, not revelation in its technical religious sense.
rows.anchor: The word “revelation” here does not refer to its meaning as a term. It means to implant a thought in the heart.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives wrongdoers respite while reassuring the upright through trials; this assurance strengthens them so hardships carry little weight.
rows.anchor: he also sounds assurance and glad tidings to the former

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph was assured that his trial would be temporary and that he would later confront his brothers from a position they could not recognize; verse 90 gives details.
rows.anchor: Time will come when he will inform his brothers about their evil deed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers probably returned late at night to prevent Jacob from having a chance to search for Joseph.
rows.anchor: The reason that the brothers came back late in the night probably was to rule out any chance of going in search of him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istibāq means racing one another; a later verse uses it for two people running toward a door.
rows.anchor: The word إﺳﺘﺒﺎقmeans  competing against one another in a race.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wolf story was a weak, unintelligent excuse chosen because Jacob had already voiced that fear, and the brothers themselves doubted he would believe it.
rows.anchor: The excuse presented by the brothers was a rather poor one and did nor reflect any intelligence in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwalat means Satan made something seem attractive, easy, and acceptable to a person.
rows.anchor: Satan seem a certain thing seem fair to them as well as very acceptable too

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For “beautiful patience,” Islahi prefers treating the phrase as an inchoative with its predicate suppressed; an alternative makes it the predicate of a suppressed inchoative, and suppression focuses attention.
rows.anchor: I have preferred the first of these.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful patience is free of complaint, grumbling, and wailing.
rows.anchor: This patience referred to is one that does not have any element of complaint, grumbling and wailing in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic account contrasts Jacob's graceful patience with the Torah's depiction of him tearing his clothes, wearing sackcloth, and mourning for many days.
rows.anchor: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and mourned for his son many days

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warada literally describes someone stepping into a spring or fountain; here it means the caravan's appointed water-fetcher.
rows.anchor: here it is used for the person who was deputed by the people of the caravan to arrange for water

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Slave trading was common, and the caravaners tried to conceal their plan to sell Joseph so that no one else could claim him.
rows.anchor: Slave trading was common in those days and the people of the caravan thought of selling Joseph (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravaners expected to profit from a slave, while God was using the episode to pave Joseph's way to become Egypt's king.
rows.anchor: They thought they would earn some money from a slave, while God was paving the way for Joseph (sws) to become the king of Egypt.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḍlāl means rendering efforts fruitless; verse 1 of Sūrah Muḥammad uses it for deeds being brought to nothing.
rows.anchor: the word إﺿﻶﻹلmeans to render efforts into nothing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Unjust to their souls” refers to polytheists, since the Qur’an identifies polytheism as the greatest injustice.
rows.anchor: polytheism is the greatest injustice according to the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can carry out whatever He wills; none can thwart Him, and intercession cannot avail before Him.
rows.anchor: None can stop Him in implementing His will nor can intercession be of avail before Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's will and intention remain governed by justice and wisdom.
rows.anchor: God’s will and intention is always governed by His justice and wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage warns Quraysh leaders of Hell for leading their people to destruction, then gives Muslims glad tidings and guidance for preparing for success.
rows.anchor: the Quraysh are explicitly warned that since they have led their people to the pit of destruction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Have you not seen” conveys amazement and grandeur; here it rebukes Quraysh leaders for leading their people toward disbelief and polytheism.
rows.anchor: Here the context shows that that it expresses amazement and rebuke and is directed at the leaders of the Quraysh.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls favors God gave Quraysh through Abraham's supplication: custodianship of the Kaʿbah, regional leadership, settled life, security, and provision in barren land.
rows.anchor: Because of being the custodians of the House of God, God granted them the leadership of all Arabia.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of valuing these gifts, Quraysh embraced polytheism and diverted people to invented deities; their respite would soon end.
rows.anchor: Instead of valuing these favours, they became engrossed in polytheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilāl means friendship or brotherhood and can also refer to barter, where each party is both buyer and seller.
rows.anchor: When things are bartered both parties are buyers and sellers at the same time.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Quraysh's warning, the address turns to Muslims; secret spending expresses sincerity, open spending motivates others, and the order gives secrecy higher status.
rows.anchor: Since spending secretly is mentioned first, it indicates that this type of spending has a higher status.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending serves the giver's own salvation and will be of use in the hereafter, rather than being primarily for others.
rows.anchor: It is not primarily needed for others. It is required for the salvation of those who spend.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording, style, and occasion also give Muslims glad tidings about their future.
rows.anchor: it gives glad tidings to the Muslims in their future.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh have failed their trust as heirs of Abraham, while believers can prepare to fulfill its aims and become worthy trustees.
rows.anchor: Believers now have a chance to prepared themselves for these objectives and to be worthy trustees.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are not deities; the author asks whether they are instead controlled by the universe's powerful, knowledgeable ruler.
rows.anchor: this make them deities or ones which are controlled by the powerful and knowledgeable ruler of this universe?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God gives people what they ask for addresses humanity in its capacity as human beings.
rows.anchor: The words “and has given you from everything you asked for” address human beings in their capacity of being human beings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fit between human demand and provision is strong evidence that the Creator arranged for every human need.
rows.anchor: The complete correspondence between demand and supply is the greatest evidence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that the general wording is used because the idolaters are unworthy of direct address for their conduct.
rows.anchor: Since they are not worthy of being addressed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies whatever human nature and physical form need, in keeping with wisdom; the match between needs and provision shows the Creator provides for all needs.
rows.anchor: whatever their nature and physical form needs is provided to them by God in accordance with His wisdom and expediency

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though phrased generally, “human beings” refers here to the idolaters discussed earlier; the general wording reflects their unworthiness because of their conduct.
rows.anchor: it refers to the idolaters which are being discussed since the previous verses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓalūm describes one who usurps rights; polytheism violates both God's right and the person's own soul.
rows.anchor: When a person indulges in polytheism, he not only usurps the right of God but also of his one soul.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaffār means ungrateful: thanking someone other than the one who actually bestowed the favor.
rows.anchor: He is a person who thanks someone other than the one from whom he has received favours.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's main defense of polytheism was that they inherited it from Abraham; the coming passage refutes that claim.
rows.anchor: The biggest argument cited by the Quraysh in favour of their polytheism was that they had inherited it from Abraham (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham settled his descendants in barren land after leaving a fertile region so they could establish a monotheistic worship center and avoid polytheism.
rows.anchor: he had settled his progeny in a desolate and barren piece of land after he had migrated from a lush and green region.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sustenance of barren Mecca came from Abraham's supplications, but Quraysh attributed these favors to idols while claiming to follow Abraham.
rows.anchor: The sustenance and livelihood found in this barren land are the sole result of Abraham’s (sws) supplications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah urges the Prophet to remain patient with adversaries and await God's judgment; if they refuse his message, their fate is near.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is urged to show patience on the attitude of his adversaries and to wait for God’s decision

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is directed to pray and supplicate for the patience needed to endure, while the harms of impatience are explained.
rows.anchor: He has been directed to diligently pray

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole sūrah addresses the Prophet; references to his opponents remain indirect.
rows.anchor: The whole of the sūrah addresses the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the previous sūrah's many prophets, this sūrah details Moses' life to guide Muhammad through his current and future preaching stages.
rows.anchor: many celebrated prophets of God are mentioned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 1–8 tell the Prophet not to overburden himself trying to secure faith from everyone; he should remind those who have some fear.
rows.anchor: His responsibility is to only remind those who have some fear in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is the Creator's directive, not a petition; the Prophet should present it with dignity, avoid pampering arrogant ingrates, and trust his Lord's knowledge.
rows.anchor: it is the directive of the creator of the heavens and the earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Moses begins with his return from Midian to the sacred valley of Ṭuwā, where he receives prophethood.
rows.anchor: Moses (sws) reaches the sacred valley

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account proceeds through Moses' first prophetic directive, signs, mission to Pharaoh, and accepted prayer for inner strength and Aaron's help.
rows.anchor: He receives his first directive after being made a prophet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God knows everything hidden and open, He will ease the Prophet's path and guide him; any delay serves a reason and his benefit.
rows.anchor: when his Lord is aware of all his secrets, his path would be eased out by Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse tells Muhammad to rely entirely on God instead of overexerting himself to reform his enemies; no other deity or support is needed.
rows.anchor: This verse directs the Prophet (sws) to completely rely on God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's good names assure the Prophet that God's attributes will protect and aid him according to his circumstances; he can seek support through any of them.
rows.anchor: all good attributes belong to God

rows.speaker: All scholars
rows.claim: Scholars agree that God's names here mean His attributes, since His names express His attributes.
rows.anchor: All scholars agree that here “names of God” actually refer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Moses account makes the assurance about God's attributes concrete by showing how God helped him through trials before and after prophethood.
rows.anchor: details of how God helped him in the trials he passed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' story foreshadows phases Muhammad had yet to face and indicates the preparation needed; one prophet's lived account serves another as a biography.
rows.anchor: The impact of living examples is unparalleled.
